supporting_observations.claim: The alerted periodic HTTPS activity is associated with ledgerlinkupd.exe running as max.fischer from the user's AppData\Local\LedgerLink directory; process creation is recorded at 13:38:50 and the process later exits at 14:09:24.

The proxy records repeated CONNECT requests to update.ledgerlink.co:443 at approximately five-minute intervals: 13:39, 13:44, 13:48, 13:54, 13:58, 14:04, and 14:09 UTC. The first is a gateway error; subsequent recorded requests succeed as tunnels.
Endpoint network records associate the later proxy connections with ledgerlinkupd.exe (PID 5392) connecting to the internal proxy at 10.55.20.30:8080.

The observed hostname is update.ledgerlink.co, whereas the supplied inventory says the approved LedgerLink updater checks update.ledgerlink.com about every five minutes and identifies its approved path as C:\Program Files\LedgerLink\ledgerlinkupd.exe. The hostname and executable location therefore differ from the inventory; this is suspicious but does not by itself establish maliciousness.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy CONNECT records show requested hostnames, status, and tunnel byte counts, but do not establish the contents or purpose of the TLS traffic.
The available records do not show the DNS resolution, destination IP, TLS certificate, or server identity for update.ledgerlink.co.
No file hash, signature validation, installation provenance, or vendor confirmation is provided for the AppData LedgerLink executable.
The available evidence covers only the specified host and time window; it does not establish whether the same executable or destination is seen elsewhere.
claims_not_established: Whether update.ledgerlink.co is controlled by or authorized for LedgerLink, or is an impersonation of the approved update.ledgerlink.com domain.
Whether the executable is a legitimate LedgerLink updater, an unauthorized copy, or malicious software.
Whether any downloaded content was executed, installed, or otherwise caused harm.
Whether the TLS sessions carried update checks, software, or other data.
additional_evidence_needed: Validate update.ledgerlink.co ownership and relationship to the approved LedgerLink service with the software vendor or through trusted domain and certificate records.
Acquire and inspect the executable, including its hash, digital signature, file metadata, and installation or download provenance.
Obtain endpoint or proxy TLS inspection evidence, if available, and correlate the tunnel contents and downloaded files with the updater process.
Check DNS, proxy, and endpoint telemetry for this domain and executable on other hosts and outside the review window.
unrelated_findings: Cisco AnyConnect vpnagent.exe started on WS-MFISCHER-01 at 13:45:01, although the supplied environment context says there is no VPN. This record shows process start, not a VPN connection; track separately and do not use it to decide the alerted activity. (T245-00148, T245-00149)

A UserAssist registry value on WS-MFISCHER-01 contains a ROT13-encoded path corresponding to mstsc.exe. This suggests a recorded Remote Desktop client entry but does not establish a remote session; investigate separately. (T245-00162)
